title: Newsom Taps Indian-American Rohit Chopra to Lead California's New Consumer Agency
excerpt: The former CFPB director will run a powerful new state regulator created to counter Trump-era federal rollbacks on consumer protection.
body:
**The Appointment:** California Governor Gavin Newsom has named Rohit Chopra, the former director of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, as the inaugural secretary of the state's new Business and Consumer Services Agency. The agency, set to launch on July 1, 2026, consolidates oversight of consumer protection across healthcare, financial services, and technology — positioning California as the primary regulatory backstop against what Newsom called 'Trump-era rollbacks' of federal consumer safeguards.

Chopra, 43, served as CFPB director from 2021 to 2025, where he earned a reputation as one of Washington's most aggressive financial regulators. Under his leadership, the bureau took on big tech companies over data privacy, cracked down on junk fees in banking, and pursued enforcement actions against predatory lenders. His appointment signals that California intends to fill the regulatory vacuum left by the current administration's deregulatory push.

**The Agency's Scope:** The Business and Consumer Services Agency will absorb several existing state departments including the Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control, the Department of Cannabis Control, and key consumer protection functions currently scattered across multiple agencies. Chopra will have authority over financial services regulation, data privacy enforcement, and healthcare pricing oversight — making this one of the most powerful state-level consumer protection posts in America.

**The Diaspora Connection:** Chopra's appointment adds another prominent name to the growing list of Indian-Americans in senior government positions across the country. Born to Indian immigrant parents, Chopra graduated from Harvard and the Wharton School before entering public service. His career arc — from FTC commissioner to CFPB director to California's top consumer regulator — reflects the increasing political influence of the Indian-American community, which punches well above its demographic weight in American governance.

**What to Watch:** The new agency launches July 1 with an ambitious mandate to lower costs and crack down on corporate abuse. Chopra's first major test will likely involve California's ongoing battles with tech companies over data privacy and AI regulation — areas where the state has positioned itself as the de facto national standard-setter.
